title: Introduce soft-reservoir token pacer and speculative kernel warmup to reduce streaming tail latency
author: Maya Chen
body: Motivation: streaming short-to-medium responses still show p95/p99 spikes when emission interleaves with kernel loads and KV rewarm. Existing credit-gated flush mechanisms control burstiness but can cause conservative flushing under variable workloads. This PR implements a soft-reservoir token pacer combined with speculative kernel warmup and adaptive KV prefetch hints to reduce tail TTFB while preserving throughput and batching efficiency. Design summary: 1) Soft-reservoir pacer: maintain a soft window of emission credits that decays gracefully instead of hard tokens; credits are replenished on token acknowledgement and rebalanced by observed latency jitter. The pacer uses a leaky-bucket shaped allocator to allow short bursts without triggering full flushes. 2) Speculative kernel warmup: when the pacer predicts an imminent microbatch flush (based on prefix patterns, recent emission cadence, and model-specific heuristics), it issues lightweight kernel priming calls that prepare the most likely attention kernels and load partial KV slices to L2 where applicable. Warmup is throttled to avoid evicting active microbatches. 3) Adaptive KV prefetch hints: runtime exposes passive hints from the pacer to the KV layer indicating expected upcoming sequence lengths and token ranges; KV service responds with prioritized partial slices and an optional low-priority rewarm path. 4) Scheduler integration: the emission scheduler uses a short-term predictor to align microbatch formation with kernel-warmup windows so that warmed kernels are used by the next flush. This maintains batching and avoids single-token kernel churn. Implementation notes: changes span emitter (runtime/emitter/pacer.go), kernel loader (runtime/kernel/priming.cu + runtime/kernel/loader.go), KV prefetch (runtime/kv/prefetch.go), and scheduler glue (runtime/scheduler/pacer_integration.go). Key algorithms are parameterized behind feature flags and dynamically tunable thresholds accessible via the console. Testing and validation: added unit tests for pacer logic and predictive windowing, end-to-end streaming bench harnesses that emulate diverse client inter-arrival patterns, and stress tests against KV eviction to ensure no regression in throughput. Benchmarks: synthetic CLI streaming benchmark (single-stream 32-token prompts, cold and warm variants) shows median first-byte latency improvement of 18% and p99 improvement of 28% in warm-path runs compared to main baseline. Multi-tenant microbatch workloads retained within 3% throughput variance. Canaries: rollout gated behind feature flag soft_reservoir_pacer with percentage-based canary and auto-fallback to previous strategy on SLO regressions. Rollout plan: enable 5% of traffic for 48h, evaluate cost/latency/throughput metrics, then ramp to 25% and 100% if regressions are within acceptable bounds. Operator controls: console exposes pacer aggressiveness slider and a diagnostic trace log for pacer decisions. Backwards compatibility: no client-facing API changes. Migration: none. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration streaming bench - [x] KV interaction tests - [x] docs update - [x] perf benchmarks in PR comments - [x] canary rollout plan Related work: complements ENG-8672 kernel primer work and ENG-9121 KV warmup heuristics. Links: internal linear ENG-1428 for rollout tracking and doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1428/soft-reservoir-pacer , design doc https://redwood-internal/docs/emit-pacer-design .

review_comments: Liam Patel: Nice end-to-end. Two questions: how do we bound warmup IO so it doesn't evict useful KV pages?
Maya Chen: We cap speculative prefetch to a configurable budget per-GPU and prefer partial slices. Added tests that simulate eviction scenarios.
Noah Rivera: Can we get a knob that forces deterministic pacer behavior for replay during debugging?
Maya Chen: Added deterministic mode under flags for replayable traces.
Sofia Gupta: Please include more metrics so SRE can set alerts (pacer_rewarm_eviction_count, pacer_skipped_warmups).
Maya Chen: Added metrics and dashboard link in docs.
CI: perf bench initially failed due to nondeterministic test seed; reran with fixed seeds and passed.
Liam Patel: approved after addressing warmup cap and metrics.
release_notes: Runtime: introduce soft-reservoir token pacer with speculative kernel warmup and adaptive KV prefetch to reduce streaming tail latency (p99) for short/mid-length streams. Configurable via console; rollout behind feature flag.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about warmup I/O; warmup is disabled by default on lower tier instances. Operator docs include recommended budgets per instance type.
